title: Add angular lock (rigid weld / fixed joint) option to PinJoint2D
body:
Addresses godotengine/godot-proposals#86

Adds an optional rigid angular lock to `PinJoint2D`, turning the pin from a free hinge into a rigid weld: the two pinned bodies keep their own collision shapes but a fixed relative orientation, so they move and topple as one rigid unit. This is the 2D "Glue Joint" / "Fixed Joint" requested in proposal #86 — a `PinJoint2D` already locks relative *position*; this adds the relative *rotation* lock, completing a fixed joint for 2D.

New API on `PinJoint2D`:

- `angular_lock_enabled: bool` (default `false`) — enable the rigid weld.
- `angular_lock_softness: float` (default `0.0`) — how quickly the weld restores its locked orientation; `0` snaps back in one step, higher springs back more softly (same sense as `softness`).
- `angular_lock_play: float` (default `0.0`) — angular deadzone (radians); the weld heals back toward alignment but stops this much short, leaving a tunable permanent free play.

Plumbed through `PhysicsServer2D` as a new `PinJointFlag` (`PIN_JOINT_FLAG_ANGULAR_LOCK_ENABLED`, appended = value 2) and two `PinJointParam`s (`PIN_JOINT_ANGULAR_LOCK_SOFTNESS`, `_PLAY`).

Implementation:

The 2D pin solver is single-phase (velocity only). A restoring term on the real velocity channel is unstable: there is nowhere to bleed the injected correction energy, so under sustained load the relative angle walks past ±π and settles flipped 180°. So this uses a Box2D-style split impulse:

1. The real velocity channel drives the relative angular velocity → 0 (kills spin, injects no energy, never flips).
2. The biased (pseudo-velocity) channel — the same split-impulse channel the contact solver uses for penetration recovery, reset every step in `integrate_forces`, integrated into orientation in `integrate_velocities` — carries the restoring term, healing the residual angle geometrically without it becoming real spin.

New helper `GodotBody2D::apply_bias_torque_impulse()`. Heal fraction per step is `1/(1+softness)` (≤1, so no overshoot); `play` is subtracted from the error magnitude before healing.

How tested:

Tested extensively in 2D scenes with real falling/colliding `RigidBody2D` bodies. With two boxes welded:

- Rigid (`softness=0`): after an external knock rotates one body ~86° out of alignment, the relative angle recovers to <1° within ~2 physics frames and the bodies thereafter move as one unit.
- Softness sweep: recovery time increases monotonically with `softness` (snap-back at `0`, progressively softer spring-back for higher values), always settling back to the locked orientation.
- Play: with `angular_lock_play` set, the weld settles at exactly that residual angle instead of fully realigning.
- No flip: the relative angle never runs away to ±180°, including under sustained gravity load on a cantilevered (overhanging) welded pair and under repeated hard knocks.
- Chains of welded bodies remain stable at arbitrary length.

This PR was developed with AI assistance and tested extensively by me; all code was reviewed by me and no copyrighted/copied code was introduced.
